Ways to work

On your own

One person, no team, and optionally no GitHub at all. What works, what quietly needs GitHub, and what that costs you.

On this page
  • Set it up
  • What works without GitHub
  • What needs GitHub
  • Alone, with GitHub

You can use Sigma alone, on a laptop, with the to-do list as plain files in your repository and no GitHub account involved. The loop takes a goal, works it through the same seven phases, runs your tests and records the outcome. What you give up is the pull request, the review on it and the automatic merge, because those are GitHub features.

Set it up

/sigma-init --mode local-goals

Add --local-only when the repository has no usable remote. The loop then edits your checkout directly, with no worktree, branch, push or pull request. If you do have a remote, leave that flag off and keep the per-goal worktree.

What works without GitHub

CapabilityHow it behaves alone
BacklogFiles in .sdlc/goals/. A goal moves pending, in_progress, done or parked in its frontmatter. Order is priority, then filename.
OrderingA goal whose body says **Blocked by:** a goal id or file stem is not picked until that goal is done.
Both run modes/sigma-goal with you at each gate, /sigma-loop on the whole backlog.
Proofverify.command and verify.enforce work the same. record done is refused without fresh evidence.
ParkingA goal that needs a person lands in .sdlc/state/review-queue.md. To resume one, change its status back to pending by hand. There is no /sigma-unpark for local goals.
LimitsBudgets, the hand-off at 20 goals, and the resource guard apply as on any run.
Visibility/sigma-status, /sigma-log, /sigma-time read local files.

What needs GitHub

CapabilityWhy
Issues as the backlog, labels, priority labelsThey are GitHub issues. Needs gh, logged in.
A pull request per goal, the post-PR review and the merge gateThey read the pull request's real state on GitHub.
work.auto_merge, --land, /sigma-orchestrateThey merge or start sessions through GitHub.
A Projects boardCreated and moved through GitHub.
Hand-offs that open an issue in someone's areaAn issue-less hand-off exists, but it is only useful with a team.
Local does not mean offline

The backlog and the records stay in your repository and Sigma reports no usage data. Your agent host still sends prompts to its model provider; that traffic is the host's, not Sigma's. See Trust and limits.

Alone, with GitHub

With GitHub as the source, the loop limits itself to issues assigned to you, so a shared repository does not hand you your colleagues' goals. The ledger is optional for one person; turn it on only when a second person or a second machine joins. See As a team.

Technical detail

Two concurrent sessions on one machine are still protected from picking the same goal: a local file lock closes the same-instant, same-machine case whether or not the ledger is on. The broader check, that a goal is already claimed by another live process, needs the ledger on to have a claim to compare against. Concurrent goals multiply memory use: size parallel.goals.max_concurrent to your RAM, not to your backlog.
